issues.title: Better Campfires incompatibility
issues.body:
### Version Information

Lithium 0.11.4 for Fabric 1.20.1

### Expected Behavior

The [Better Campfires](https://modrinth.com/mod/better-campfires) mod causes campfires to extinguish over time, and you can click the campfire with an empty hand to see approximately how much time is left. This number continually ticks down to zero, when the campfire goes out.

### Actual Behavior

With Lithium installed, the number remains static and the campfire never extinguishes.

### Reproduction Steps

1) Install Better Campfires
2) Install Lithium
3) Place campfire, right-click
4) Observe the time left until it goes out

issues.title: Framed maps never drop players who left or died from `carriedByPlayers` (memory leak with `mixin.entity.framed_maps`)

labels.name: F-has-workaround
labels.description: Flag: There is a workaround available

issues.body:
### Version Information

lithium-fabric-0.26.2+mc26.3 (Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3, Minecraft 26.3).

### Expected Behavior

A map in an item frame drops players from `MapItemSavedData.carriedByPlayers` / `carriedBy` once they are removed (left the server or died), like vanilla.

### Actual Behavior

With `mixin.entity.framed_maps` enabled, framed maps never drop removed players. Every player who was in the dimension while a framed map ticked stays in that map's `carriedByPlayers` for good, and the whole old `ServerPlayer` object stays reachable: inventory, advancements, stats.

On our server (25 players online, 19.4 h uptime, ~380 map-art maps in item frames) a heap dump showed:
- 379 `ServerPlayer` objects: 316 with removal reason `UNLOADED_WITH_PLAYER`, 41 `KILLED`;
- 109,410 `MapItemSavedData$HoldingPlayer` objects;
- about 600 MB retained, growing by roughly 30 MB per hour.

The GC-root path for the old players went through `MapItemSavedData.carriedByPlayers` (in the `SavedDataStorage` cache). With `mixin.entity.framed_maps=false` the count stays flat.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Fabric API + Lithium (+ Carpet, only to create fake players).
2. Make a filled map and put it in an item frame in a loaded chunk.
3. Keep one player online in the same dimension.
4. Have other players join and leave 20 times; any player works, we used `/player VisitorN spawn` then `/player VisitorN kill`.
5. `jcmd <pid> GC.class_histogram | grep HoldingPlayer`

| Setup | `HoldingPlayer` after step 5 |
|---|---|
| vanilla + Fabric API + Carpet | 1 |
| + VMP | 1–2 |
| + Lithium | 22, never shrinks, even after the online player walks up to the frame |
| + Lithium, `mixin.entity.framed_maps=false` | 1–2 |

### Other Information

Cause: [`MapItemSavedDataMixin` L27–L42](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium/blob/38104b18fa0f21d8e04e0599ce3ee2bb0566bd58/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/lithium/mixin/entity/framed_maps/MapItemSavedDataMixin.java#L27-L42)

For framed maps (`placedInFrame != null`) the mixin makes the `carriedBy` loop in `tickCarriedBy` run once and only over the ticking player's own holder:
- `sizeOrOne` ([L31–L33](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium/blob/38104b18fa0f21d8e04e0599ce3ee2bb0566bd58/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/lithium/mixin/entity/framed_maps/MapItemSavedDataMixin.java#L31-L33)) returns 1;
- `getOrGetThePlayer` ([L39–L42](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium/blob/38104b18fa0f21d8e04e0599ce3ee2bb0566bd58/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/lithium/mixin/entity/framed_maps/MapItemSavedDataMixin.java#L39-L42)) returns `carriedByPlayers.get(player)`.

That loop is the only place vanilla prunes holders, and only through its `else` branch:

```java
// MapItemSavedData.tickCarriedBy (vanilla 26.3)
for (int i = 0; i < this.carriedBy.size(); i++) {           // Lithium: 1 for framed maps
    HoldingPlayer other = this.carriedBy.get(i);              // Lithium: the ticking player's holder
    Player otherPlayer = other.player;
    if (!otherPlayer.isRemoved() && (placedInFrame != null || otherPlayer.getInventory().contains(mapMatcher))) {
        ...
    } else {
        this.carriedByPlayers.remove(otherPlayer);            // never reached for framed maps:
        this.carriedBy.remove(other);                         // the ticking player is never removed
        this.removeDecoration(otherName);
    }
}
```

`ServerEntity.sendChanges` calls `tickCarriedBy` every 10 ticks with each player in the level for every framed map. So every player gets added to every framed map, and nobody who left is ever removed. The dump also had 41 retained `KILLED` players, but we did not reproduce deaths separately (a fake player dying 15 times next to the frame only raised the count from 1 to 3), so treat deaths as unconfirmed.

The vanilla path for framed maps never scans other players' inventories (`placedInFrame != null` short-circuits), so pruning removed holders in the frame branch should cost almost nothing. A possible fix: keep the frame shortcut, but still drop holders whose player `isRemoved()`.

Other mods on the server: Fabrolia, C2ME, VMP, ServerCore, Carpet and others, but the leak reproduces with only Fabric API + Lithium (+ Carpet for fake players).

issues.title: Hopper under a double chest only pulls from the half above it if that half was placed with chest type already set
issues.body:
### Version Information

lithium-fabric-0.26.2+mc26.3 (Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3, Minecraft 26.3). Same result with lithium-fabric-0.25.3+mc26.2 on 26.2.

### Expected Behavior

A hopper under one half of a double chest pulls items from both halves.

### Actual Behavior

The hopper only pulls from the half directly above it. This happens when the half above the hopper is placed already as part of a double chest (type=left or right) while the other half does not exist yet. Items in the other half are never taken. Breaking and replacing the hopper, or reloading the chunk, fixes it.

### Reproduction Steps

1. `/setblock 0 63 0 minecraft:barrel`
2. `/setblock 0 64 0 minecraft:hopper[facing=down]`
3. `/setblock 0 65 0 minecraft:chest[type=left,facing=north]`
4. Wait a second or two so the hopper ticks.
5. `/setblock 1 65 0 minecraft:chest[type=right,facing=north]`
6. `/item replace block 1 65 0 container.13 with minecraft:diamond 3`

With Lithium the diamonds stay in the chest. With only Fabric API they end up in the barrel.

### Other Information

Reproduced with only Fabric API and Lithium installed.

Placing chests by hand doesn't trigger this, because the first chest is single and turns into the left half when the second one is placed. Servux's easy place handler accepts chest_type from the client, though, so a player using Litematica Easy Place or the printer can place the half above the hopper first, with its type already set from the schematic. On our server that
gave us double chests over hoppers that only emptied one half, and nobody used commands.

My guess at the cause: the hopper caches the single chest it found (extractBlockInventory). The second half is diagonal to the hopper and the chest above keeps its state, so nothing clears that cache.

issues.title: [Server thread/WARN] Entity cannot be analysed. [NeoForge | 1.21.1]

labels.name: F-has-workaround
labels.description: Flag: There is a workaround available

issues.body:
Interaction with mod NoMansLand, entity : buddy

[Server thread/WARN] [Lithium Class Analysis/]: Lithium Class Analysis Error: Class com.farcr.nomansland.common.entity.buddy.Buddy cannot be analysed, because getting declared methods crashes with NoClassDefFoundError: net/minecraft/client/model/geom/ModelPart. This is usually caused by modded entities declaring methods that have a return type or parameter type that is annotated with @Environment(value=EnvType.CLIENT). Loading the type is not possible, because it only exists in the CLIENT environment. The recommended fix is to annotate the method with this argument or return type with the same annotation. Lithium handles this error by assuming the class cannot be included in some optimizations.

issues.title: GameEventDispatcherStorage retains LevelChunks forever — memory leak when chunks unload (mixin.world.game_events.dispatch)
issues.body:
# Issue: `[NeoForge] GameEventDispatcherStorage retains LevelChunks forever — memory leak when chunks unload (mixin.world.game_events.dispatch)`

**Reported against:** lithium-neoforge `0.15.4+mc1.21.1` (official CaffeineMC build)

---

## Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| Minecraft | 1.21.1 |
| NeoForge | 21.1.250 |
| Lithium | 0.15.4+mc1.21.1 |
| Java | 21 (dedicated server, Windows 11 x64) |
| Heap | 16 GB (`-Xmx16G`) |
| Worldgen | Big Globe (builderb0y) world generator |
| Workload amplifier | Chunky chunk pre-generator (used to make the leak visible quickly — plain exploration reproduces it, just much slower) |

## Summary

When `mixin.world.game_events.dispatch` is enabled, **every `LevelChunk` that has ever been loaded is held by a strong reference inside lithium's `GameEventDispatcherStorage` and is never released on chunk unload**. The server leaks roughly the full loaded-chunk population permanently; after a pre-generation run of ~41k chunks the heap was 88.4% retained `LevelChunk` instances and full GCs could not reclaim anything.

## Symptom

- MAT Leak Suspects on a 12.8 GB heap dump: **41,359 instances of `LevelChunk` retaining 12,143,806,488 bytes (88.38%)**.
- Pausing chunk generation does **not** help: chunk retention count stayed frozen at 17,668 for 8+ minutes with zero players online and nothing loading new terrain.
- Full GCs (`System.gc()` via `jcmd`) reclaim only a few thousand instances of temporary noise; the bulk never leaves the `Long2ReferenceOpenHashMap` described below.

## Root cause (evidence)

MAT *Merge Shortest Paths to GC Roots* on a 10,000-sample of retained `LevelChunk`s shows **9,975 instances reachable through a single path**:

```
Server thread
 └─ MinecraftServer (DedicatedServer)
     └─ ServerLevel[8][0]                        (overworld)
         └─ LithiumData$Data                     (net.caffeinemc.mods.lithium.common.world.LithiumData)
             └─ GameEventDispatcherStorage
                 └─ Long2ReferenceOpenHashMap    (table: Object[32769], grown)
                     └─ per-section Int2ObjectOpenHashMap listeners
                         └─ LevelChunk  ← held forever
```

Relevant mixins (from the 0.15.4 jar / Force-disable log):

- `world.game_events.dispatch.GameEventDispatcherMixin`
- `world.game_events.dispatch.LevelChunkMixin`

The storage is keyed per section and appears to be populated on chunk load, but **nothing removes the entries when a chunk unloads on NeoForge** — the section → listener map keeps a strong reference chain to the chunk itself. Suspected NeoForge port gap: no chunk-unload hook wired into this storage.

## Reproduction

1. Dedicated server, NeoForge 21.1.250 + lithium 0.15.4 (default config).
2. Load terrain (teleport around or run `chunky start`), then unload it (teleport away / `chunky pause`).
3. Count live chunks: `jcmd <pid> GC.class_histogram | grep net.minecraft.world.level.chunk.LevelChunk`.
4. Expected: instance count drops back toward spawn-radius levels after unload + GC. Observed: count is pinned at the high-water mark indefinitely.

## Control experiment (proves the mixin is the culprit)

Added to `config/lithium.properties`:

```
mixin.world.game_events.dispatch=false
```

Restarted, re-ran the **same** Chunky workload at full speed (~27 GB/s allocation rate observed):

- Startup log confirms: `world.game_events.dispatch.GameEventDispatcherMixin` and `world.game_events.dispatch.LevelChunkMixin` were Force-disabled.
- Chunk retention now oscillates normally (464 → 440 → 914 across samples) instead of pinning at the high-water mark.
- Heap stays stable around **1.6 GB** where it previously ballooned past 12 GB and wedged.

## Expected fix

`GameEventDispatcherStorage` (and/or `LevelChunkMixin`) must drop section entries on chunk unload, matching Fabric behavior — or the NeoForge port should be audited for a missing unload hook.

## Workaround (until fixed)

```
# config/lithium.properties
mixin.world.game_events.dispatch=false
```

Cost: game-event listening dispatch loses the lithium optimization (vibration sensors / sculk mechanics run on vanilla path). Acceptable for affected servers.

---

# Appendix: Full Environment

## Machine

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Hardware | ASUS TUF Gaming F15 (FX507ZR) laptop |
| CPU | 12th Gen Intel Core i7-12700H (14C/20T, 6P+8E) |
| RAM | 32 GB (31.6 GB usable) |
| OS | Windows 11 (build 26200), x64 |
| Java | Eclipse Temurin 21.0.12.1+1 LTS, HotSpot 64-Bit Server VM |

## JVM arguments (user_jvm_args.txt)

```
-Xms14G
-Xmx14G
-XX:+UseG1GC
-XX:+ParallelRefProcEnabled
-XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200
-XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions
-XX:+DisableExplicitGC
-XX:+AlwaysPreTouch
-XX:G1NewSizePercent=40
-XX:G1MaxNewSizePercent=50
-XX:G1HeapRegionSize=16M
-XX:G1ReservePercent=15
-XX:G1HeapWastePercent=5
-XX:G1MixedGCCountTarget=4
-XX:InitiatingHeapOccupancyPercent=20
-XX:G1MixedGCLiveThresholdPercent=90
-XX:G1RSetUpdatingPauseTimePercent=5
-XX:SurvivorRatio=32
-XX:MaxTenuringThreshold=1
-XX:+PerfDisableSharedMem
-Xlog:gc*:file=logs/gc.log:time,uptime,level,tags:filecount=5,filesize=10M
```

Note: the leak reproduces with default `-Xmx16G`/plain G1 flags too — the args above were only tuned afterwards.

## Relevant server.properties values

```
level-type=bigglobe:bigglobe
view-distance=10
simulation-distance=10
max-tick-time=0
sync-chunk-writes=true
spawn-protection=0
difficulty=hard
```

## Lithium config

`config/lithium.properties` was **default (empty)** at the time of the leak. After diagnosis, the single line below was added (this is the workaround, not the repro state):

```
mixin.world.game_events.dispatch=false
```

issues.title: Comparator output remains stale after hopper empties chest with hopper optimization enabled

labels.name: F-has-workaround
labels.description: Flag: There is a workaround available

issues.body:
### Version Information

Lithium: `lithium-fabric-0.15.4+mc1.21.1`  
Minecraft: `1.21.1`  
Fabric Loader: `0.19.3`  
Fabric API: `0.116.15`
Java: `Temurin-17.0.12+7`

### Expected Behavior

When a chest being read by a comparator is emptied by a hopper, the comparator output should update to signal strength 0 once the chest is empty.

### Actual Behavior

Under certain conditions, after the chest is completely emptied by a hopper, the comparator directly reading the chest does not update to signal strength 0. Instead, it remains stuck at its previous output signal strength.

The comparator itself is reading the chest directly; the relevant comparator/chest portion of the redstone circuit is identical to another working copy of the same circuit.

Breaking and replacing the comparator immediately causes it to correctly output signal strength 0.

The issue stops occurring when Lithium's hopper optimization is disabled with:

```properties
mixin.block.hopper=false
```

### Other Information

The issue was discovered while testing the item gate included with the MIS V5.1 multi-item sorter:

- Storage Catalog entry: https://storagecatalog.org/archives/MF004-MIS-V5-1/
- Exact schematic used: https://github.com/Storage-Catalog/Archive/blob/main/Archive/MF_multi-item-filters/MF004_MIS_V5.1/attachments/MF004_MIS_V5.1_2wt.litematic

The failure prevents the item gate from correctly detecting that its input chest is empty, which in turn prevents the gate from returning to its idle state.

The important observations are:

- The chest is visibly empty when the comparator remains powered.
- The comparator directly reads the chest.
- The comparator/chest portion of the circuit appears identical between the FHL and non-FHL versions of the V5.1 item gate.
- In the affected non-FHL setup, the comparator can remain at a stale non-zero output after the chest has been emptied by the hopper.
- Breaking and replacing only the comparator immediately makes it correctly output signal strength 0.
- Disabling Lithium's hopper optimization with `mixin.block.hopper=false` fixes the issue.
- With `mixin.block.hopper=false`, the same item gate and redstone setup correctly updates the comparator to 0 when the chest becomes empty.

I have not yet confirmed whether the issue reproduces with Lithium in an otherwise minimal Fabric installation.

issues.title: Client kicked with "Network Protocol Error" when a sleeping villager dies (experimental unused_brain mixin)
issues.body:
### Version

lithium-fabric-0.24.2+mc26.1.2 (Fabric, singleplayer, Windows). Shipped in the Simply Optimized Reloaded modpack, which sets `mixin.experimental=true`.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Enable Lithium's experimental mixins (`mixin.experimental=true` in `lithium.properties`), so `mixin.experimental.client_tick.entity.unused_brain` is active.
2. Kill a **sleeping** villager (for example TNT next to a house at night).
3. The client is kicked from the (integrated) server with **"Network Protocol Error"**.

### Analysis

The death entity event reaches the client, and vanilla's client-side death path writes to the villager's brain:

`ClientboundEntityEventPacket` → `Villager.handleEntityEvent` → `LivingEntity.die` → `Villager.stopSleeping` → `Brain.setMemory`

`stopSleeping` runs on both sides in vanilla, so the dummy client-side brain introduced by `mixin.experimental.client_tick.entity.unused_brain` throws its guard exception inside packet handling, which disconnects the client. Any mob whose client-side vanilla code touches brain memories on death while sleeping should trigger the same guard.

### Crash / Stacktrace

```
[Render thread/ERROR]: Failed to handle packet net.minecraft.network.protocol.game.ClientboundEntityEventPacket@6532fe94, disconnecting
java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException: Dummy client side brain memory slot cannot be modified! This is an optimization introduced by lithium. [...]
	at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.memory.MemorySlot.throwOnModifyDummyMemorySlot(MemorySlot.java:1032)
	at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.memory.MemorySlot.handler$dbi000$lithium$throwIfDummyMemorySlot(MemorySlot.java:1026)
	at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.memory.MemorySlot.set(MemorySlot.java:38)
	at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.Brain.wrapOperation$cml000$lithium$setTrackingChanges(Brain.java:1157)
	at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.Brain.setMemoryInternal(Brain.java:256)
	at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.Brain.setMemory(Brain.java:202)
	at net.minecraft.world.entity.npc.villager.Villager.stopSleeping(Villager.java:949)
	at net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity.die(LivingEntity.java:1502)
	at net.minecraft.world.entity.npc.villager.AbstractVillager.die(AbstractVillager.java:210)
	at net.minecraft.world.entity.npc.villager.Villager.die(Villager.java:625)
	at net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity.handleEntityEvent(LivingEntity.java:2107)
	at net.minecraft.world.entity.Mob.handleEntityEvent(Mob.java:367)
	at net.minecraft.world.entity.npc.villager.Villager.handleEntityEvent(Villager.java:747)
	at net.minecraft.client.multiplayer.ClientPacketListener.handleEntityEvent(ClientPacketListener.java:1245)
	at net.minecraft.network.protocol.game.ClientboundEntityEventPacket.handle(ClientboundEntityEventPacket.java:40)
	at net.minecraft.network.PacketProcessor$ListenerAndPacket.handle(PacketProcessor.java:55)
	at net.minecraft.network.PacketProcessor.processQueuedPackets(PacketProcessor.java:38)
	at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.runTick(Minecraft.java:1343)
```

Only vanilla code in the path besides the Lithium mixins; no other mod involved.

### Workaround

`mixin.experimental.client_tick.entity.unused_brain=false` in `lithium.properties`.

issues.title: Sculk sensor/shrieker miss wake on forced vibration scheduling and on loading a current vibration
issues.body:
Version Information

lithium-neoforge-0.25.2+mc26.2

Expected Behavior

A sleeping sculk sensor should wake and process a vibration when one is scheduled, including when a player steps directly on the sensor. A sculk sensor or shrieker loaded from disk with a vibration already in progress should resume processing it.

Actual Behavior

Two cases leave the block entity asleep and the vibration unprocessed:

Stepping directly on a sculk sensor schedules the vibration through a path that does not reach the wake hook, so the sensor never activates.
A block entity loaded from NBT with an already-current vibration — not merely a queued one — does not wake, and that vibration is dropped.
Reproduction Steps

For case 1:

Place a sculk sensor in a loaded chunk and let it go idle.
Step directly onto the sculk sensor block itself, rather than making a vibration nearby.
The sensor does not activate.

For case 2:

Trigger a sculk sensor or shrieker so it has a vibration in progress.
Save and quit, or unload and reload the chunk, while that vibration is still current.
On reload the vibration is never processed.
Other Information

NeoForge 26.2.0.32-beta, Java 25. No other mods installed.

Both cases were fixed in my own port by moving the wake to the shared scheduleVibration point and recognising queued and current loaded vibrations. Found alongside a similar wake omission in the sleeping furnace, which I've filed separately.

issues.title: Sleeping furnace does not wake when fuel is inserted using /item replace
issues.body:
Version Information

lithium-neoforge-0.25.2+mc26.2

Expected Behavior

A furnace containing a smeltable item should begin smelting when fuel is inserted afterwards.

Actual Behavior

The furnace remains asleep permanently and never smelts. Both the input and the fuel stay untouched indefinitely, and no output is produced.

Reproduction Steps
Place a furnace in a loaded chunk.
Insert a smeltable item into the input slot — for example raw iron. The furnace wakes, finds no fuel, and goes back to sleep.
Insert fuel into the fuel slot — for example coal.
Nothing happens. The furnace does not resume ticking, the fuel is not consumed, and no output appears.

Inserting fuel before the smeltable item works normally, so the order matters.

Other Information

NeoForge 26.2.0.32-beta, Java 25. No other mods installed.

The sleeping furnace only wakes through lithium$handleSetChanged. NeoForge's furnace fuel insertion path does not issue that setChanged notification, so the wake never fires.

I found this while working with Lithium's patches on NeoForge and confirmed it deterministically in an automated benchmark: a furnace lane produced 58 items with the sleeping optimization disabled and 0 with it enabled, across repeated runs. I have gametests covering the direct-slot case and a hopper-fed matrix (input-then-fuel, fuel-then-input, and simultaneous top-input/side-fuel hoppers); all failed before adding a wake hook on the item-set path and passed after. Happy to share those if useful.

I haven't tested the Fabric builds. Since the mechanism is specifically that NeoForge's fuel path skips the notification Lithium relies on, this may be NeoForge-only.

labels.name: S-stale
labels.description: Status: The issue has not received any feedback and has gone stale

issues.body:
When handling level_chunk_with_light packets, Lithium's count mixin in PalettedContainer (class_2841) assumes palette data is always valid and accesses palette entries without bounds checking.

If the server sends a chunk where a block references a palette index that equals or exceeds the palette size (e.g. index 11 for a palette of length 11), it throws an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and disconnects the client.

Stack trace:
java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 11 out of bounds for length 11
    at net.minecraft.class_2841.md834414$lithium$lambda$count$2$0(class_2841.java:1635)
    at net.minecraft.class_3508.method_21739(class_3508.java:213)
    at net.minecraft.class_2841.handler$ckl000$lithium$count(class_2841.java:1635)

The count mixin should add defensive bounds checking instead of trusting palette data from the server.

issues.title: Option to Suppress Crash from Accessing Chunks from Other Threads (DimThreads Compat)

labels.name: F-has-workaround
labels.description: Flag: There is a workaround available

issues.body:
Running `lithium-neoforge-0.15.3+mc1.21.1`
Crashlog - [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29325585/latest.log) (This will be very bloated because of all the reloads I was doing while working on other modpack features)

### Reproduction Steps

- Download DimThreads
- Open a Nether Portal
- Throw an item in
- Game crash

The game reports that the crash was due to the IllegalStateException thrown when non-main threads access chunks from [ChunkStatusTracker.onChunkAccessible](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium/blob/develop/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/lithium/common/world/chunk/ChunkStatusTracker.java#L50). I'm assuming this is in place to prevent potential corruption from multiple things reading/writing a chunk at the same time, but DimThreads should be allocating all of the chunk modifications to a single, alternate thread, which shouldn't cause any problems.
If it wouldn't cause any issues, it would be nice to have a config option that disables the error or changes the log level, assuming that doesn't fill the console with errors while other dimensions are loaded.

### Additional Information

There are a lot more times I've accidentally triggered this issue in non-vanilla ways (modded methods of changing dimensions), and [as I reported on the DimThreads issue page](https://github.com/SrRapero720/dimthreads/issues/58) it can sometimes cause a hang instead of a crash. I'm unsure of whether Lithium is the culprit for that issue since there were quite a few mods involved, but preventing the this error would get me a step closing to figuring that other one out.

issues.title: [NeoForge 1.21.1] entity.inactive_navigations causes NPE in Mob.getPathfindingMalus when PathType is null

labels.name: F-has-workaround
labels.description: Flag: There is a workaround available

issues.body:
## Description

On NeoForge 1.21.1 with lithium `0.15.3+mc1.21.1`, the `mixin.entity.inactive_navigations` optimization causes a server crash when a Villager attempts to pathfind. The crash is a `NullPointerException` in `Mob.getPathfindingMalus` because the `PathType` parameter is null.

This is likely related to NeoForge 1.21.1 changing `PathType` from an enum to a registry-backed object. When lithium's inactive/active navigation state switches, the path type lookup can return null in a state that vanilla never produces.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install lithium `0.15.3+mc1.21.1` on NeoForge `21.1.229`
2. Load a world with Villagers
3. Let Villagers attempt to pathfind (e.g. near a workstation or bed)
4. Server crashes

## Crash Report

```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "net.minecraft.world.level.pathfinder.PathType.getMalus()" because "p_326934_" is null
    at net.minecraft.world.entity.Mob.getPathfindingMalus(Mob.java:183)
    at net.minecraft.world.level.pathfinder.WalkNodeEvaluator.findAcceptedNode(WalkNodeEvaluator.java:234)
    at net.minecraft.world.level.pathfinder.WalkNodeEvaluator.getNeighbors(WalkNodeEvaluator.java:143)
    at net.minecraft.world.level.pathfinder.PathFinder.findPath(PathFinder.java:105)
    at net.minecraft.world.level.pathfinder.PathFinder.findPath(PathFinder.java:50)
    at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.navigation.PathNavigation.createPath(PathNavigation.java:145)
    at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.navigation.PathNavigation.createPath(PathNavigation.java:127)
    at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.navigation.PathNavigation.createPath(PathNavigation.java:112)
    at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.navigation.GroundPathNavigation.createPath(GroundPathNavigation.java:70)
    at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.behavior.MoveToTargetSink.tryComputePath(MoveToTargetSink.java:137)
    at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.behavior.MoveToTargetSink.checkExtraStartConditions(MoveToTargetSink.java:65)
    at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.behavior.Behavior.tryStart(Behavior.java:47)
    at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.Brain.startEachNonRunningBehavior(Brain.java:736)
    at net.minecraft.world.entity.ai.Brain.tick(Brain.java:492)
    at net.minecraft.world.entity.npc.Villager.customServerAiStep(Villager.java:274)
    at net.minecraft.world.entity.Mob.serverAiStep(Mob.java:785)
```

Active lithium mixins visible in the stack trace:
- `lithium.mixins.json:entity.inactive_navigations.MobMixin`
- `lithium.mixins.json:entity.inactive_navigations.PathNavigationMixin`
- `lithium.mixins.json:entity.inactive_navigations.ServerLevelMixin`

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Minecraft | 1.21.1 |
| NeoForge | 21.1.229 |
| Lithium | 0.15.3+mc1.21.1 |
| Java | 21.0.10 |

## Workaround

Add the following to `config/lithium.properties`:

```properties
mixin.entity.inactive_navigations=false
```

Disabling this specific mixin prevents the crash entirely.

issues.title: Illagers don't pick up dropped ominous banners during raids on 26.1.2
issues.body:
Version Information
lithium-fabric-0.24.2+mc26.1.2
Expected Behavior
When a wave captain dies during a raid, other nearby illagers in the same raid should path to the dropped ominous banner and one should pick it up to become the new wave captain.
Actual Behavior
With Lithium installed, illagers in the raid ignore the dropped banner entirely. No new wave captain is ever assigned — the banner stays on the ground until it despawns. Removing Lithium restores correct vanilla behavior on the same world/seed.
Reproduction Steps

Fabric 26.1.2 server with only Fabric API + Lithium installed
Verify /gamerule mobGriefing true
Stand in a village with at least one villager and a claimed bed
drink ominous bottle then wait for Raid Omen to expire to trigger a raid
Wait for a wave to spawn, kill only the wave captain (the illager wearing the banner)
Observe: surviving illagers in the wave do not path toward the dropped banner; no new captain is assigned. Banner eventually despawns.
Remove Lithium, repeat from step 3 -> vanilla behavior works as expected.

Other Information
Other mods in stack (none of these cause the bug — verified by removing Lithium alone fixes it):

fabric-api

c2me-fabric (alpha)
vmp-fabric (alpha)
noisiumforked

issues.title: 'looking_at' predicates & commands fail to pass with the latest lithium version for 26.1.2

labels.name: F-good-issue
labels.description: Flag: This is an example of a good issue report

labels.name: F-has-workaround
labels.description: Flag: There is a workaround available

issues.body:
### Version Information

lithium-fabric-0.24.2+mc26.1.2

### Expected Behavior

The predicate should pass, subsequently showing "Test Passed" in chat.

### Actual Behavior

The predicate does in fact, not pass

### Reproduction Steps

1. Go into a flat world/area
2. Summon an entity, in this case I will just be using an interaction entity for the sake of simplicity (type "/summon minecraft:interaction ~ ~ ~" in chat)
3. Make sure nothing is obstructing your's or the summoned entity's line of sight
4. Use a 'looking_at' predicate while looking at the entity, this can be done by typing "/execute if predicate {"condition":"entity_properties","entity":"this","predicate":{"type_specific":{"type":"player","looking_at":{"type":"interaction"}}}}" into chat
5. See that the predicate fails
6. Load up your same instance but without lithium, repeat the above-seen steps, and see that the predicate passes this time around

### Other Information

This was tested on the latest fabric (0.19.2) and fabric api (0.146.1) versions (with no additional mods), alongside minecraft 26.1.2

Many datapacks, minecraft maps, command block creations, and such, use predicates such as this one for their functionality, which means that this problem is currently affecting such content and creators

(While the predicate shown in the reproduction steps is an inline predicate command, this also applies to predicates ran through 'execute if predicate <predicate>' when using a datapack with a 'looking_at' predicate json)

labels.name: F-good-issue
labels.description: Flag: This is an example of a good issue report

labels.name: F-has-workaround
labels.description: Flag: There is a workaround available

issues.body:
### Version Information

lithium-fabric-0.21.4+mc1.21.11

### Expected Behavior

Explosions should not break blocks inside claimed chunks.

When using Lithium together with FTB Chunks (Fabric), chunk-claimed explosion protection does not work correctly.

Explosions (e.g. TNT) are able to destroy blocks inside claimed chunks, even though protection is enabled.

### Actual Behavior

Explosion damage is not prevented — blocks are destroyed inside claimed chunks.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Install Lithium (Fabric) v0.21.4
2. Install FTB Chunks (Fabric) v2111.1.1
3. Claim a chunk using FTB Chunks
4. Trigger an explosion (e.g. TNT) inside the claimed chunk

### Cause / workaround

The issue appears to be caused by the Lithium optimization:

mixin.world.explosions.block_raycast

Disabling it in lithium.properties fixes the issue:

mixin.world.explosions.block_raycast=false

After applying this change, FTB Chunks correctly prevents explosion damage in claimed chunks.

### Other Information

This suggests the optimized explosion raycasting may bypass or alter the logic/hooks that FTB Chunks relies on to cancel block damage.

issues.title: Lithium crashes client on corrupted chunk palette instead of safely skipping invalid entries (1.21.1 + Sodium + BetterEnd + C2ME)
issues.body:
Hi.

I’m running a heavily modded Fabric 1.21.1 environment (server + client), and I’m repeatedly hitting hard client crashes caused by Lithium when a chunk contains invalid palette entries.

Crash message:

LithiumHashPalette.missingPaletteEntryCrash
Missing Palette entry for index X


This happens during rendering (usually water), often triggered when:

• dying (camera briefly moves through blocks)
• looking through walls for a split second
• Sodium attempts fluid rendering
• BetterEnd applies biome water color

Lithium immediately throws and kills the entire client.

Important detail:
The chunk is already corrupted (null palette slots).
Lithium is not the original cause, but it is the component that hard crashes instead of handling the situation gracefully.

In my case this is most likely introduced by C2ME (Concurrent Chunk Management Engine) running on the server, which can occasionally generate corrupted chunk palettes due to aggressive multithreading.

However, regardless of the origin, the current Lithium behavior turns a recoverable world corruption into an unavoidable client crash.

This leads to situations where:

• players randomly crash when dying
• looking at water instantly closes the game
• affected chunks become impossible to approach
• long term worlds become unplayable

What I’m asking:

Instead of throwing a fatal exception on missing palette entries, could Lithium:

• replace invalid entries with air
• skip the broken section
• log a warning and continue
• or provide a config option to disable hard crashes

Right now Lithium acts as a kill switch for any corrupted chunk, even though the client could technically continue running.

For long term survival servers, this behavior is extremely destructive.

Environment:

Minecraft 1.21.1
Fabric Loader 0.18.x
Sodium present
BetterEnd present
C2ME present on server (removed on client for testing)
Large modpack (200+ mods)
Long running survival world

Removing client side C2ME reduces crash frequency, but the underlying issue remains because Lithium always aborts on palette mismatch.

Please consider making this failure mode non fatal.

Thanks.

issues.title: Compatibility Issue Between Carpet TIS and Lithium for Minecraft 1.21
issues.body: I would like to report an issue regarding the compatibility between Carpet TIS (Fabric) and Lithium for Minecraft 1.21. Currently, Carpet TIS (Fabric) in any version for Minecraft 1.21 does not support Lithium 1.4.0 or earlier versions. However, Minecraft 1.21 does not include any versions of Lithium beyond 1.4.0, which results in a compatibility gap. This means that many players are unable to use both of these mods simultaneously, which significantly limits the gameplay experience for those of us who wish to take advantage of both. We kindly request that you consider adding support for Lithium 1.4.1 (or higher versions) for Minecraft 1.21, as this would allow for compatibility between these two popular mods. Thank you for your time and consideration. We look forward to seeing this issue addressed in future updates! MC player:Likemike Mod:https://modrinth.com/mod/carpet-tis-addition

issues.title: possible improvement to ray casts for explosions
issues.body:
what i'm suggesting:
- keep the float strength = this.radius * (0.7F + (random.nextFloat() * 0.6F)) and step size, and use it to implement a random Quasi-Monte Carlo for more optimized explosions

reason:
- could help reduce the number of rays
- Less overlap: By reducing ray overlap, QMC ensures that a greater proportion of the computational work is spent on checking unique block locations.
- better cache utilization and memory usage
- using current way to introduce randomness to initial strength calculation can keep vanilla like randomness and could help preserve vanilla mechanics/parity even with qmc

issues.title: possible idea for optimizing explosions
issues.body:
i don't know if this is at all possible and i may be wrong about some of this
reason:
- block state updates can be slow, so for explosions how can they be parallelized

suggestion:
- by halving the number of rays sent out and updating the code that calls setBlockState in intersected blocks to call it with notify neighbors almost unconditionally it might be able to make some of the calls more locally and potentially parallelizable.
- the notify neighbors needs to be cancelled if the recieving block has already recieved a signal or if outside the radius(unless the block outside the radius is for example sand)

i've attached a proposed diagram of method, sorry for the poor diagram

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e6d11e2-663d-4d2c-a66f-02b97c7a03c5)

edit; may only be possible if a custom neighbor notifier signal is added, as the filter system may require to update how setBlockState works, which might be difficult and custom signalling could get around this
this would likely need to be a message passing that recursively sends out signals until a condition is met
still haven't quite worked out how to keep the energy loss calculations functionally the same as vanilla

issues.title: Lithium breaks a NeoForge patch preventing a loading deadlock caused by `ServerChunkCache::getChunk`

labels.name: F-has-workaround
labels.description: Flag: There is a workaround available

issues.body:
Minecraft: 1.21.8
NeoForge: 21.8.4-beta
Lithium: 0.18.0+mc1.21.8

[latest.log](https://mclo.gs/oZffmVg)

The Neo patch and the reasons for it is outlined here:
https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/pull/7697
https://github.com/neoforged/NeoForge/pull/99
https://github.com/neoforged/NeoForge/pull/110

To reproduce I have a mod that allows mobs (like illagers and drowneds) to spawn with equipment, which is applied during `EntityJoinLevelEvent`.

Without Lithium this works fine, with Lithium installed it is very easy to get a deadlock.

Steps for reproducing:
- Install the following mods: Lithium, Puzzles Lib, [Armored Foes](https://mega.nz/file/TMEWATKT#i9ghVMH2X--sHkpUTIEJ9pL5V16Ji-kob925G4UvGEs)
- Create  a world using the following seed: -6902519934141284895
- Run this command: `/tp @s -880 ~ -1568`
- Fly out in the ocean a bit, you will notice chunks stop generating and upon trying to leave the world via the pause screen `Saving world` will show forever. The log does not give any hint at this.

The problem is this Mixin: https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium/blob/develop/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/lithium/mixin/world/chunk_access/ServerChunkCacheMixin.java

Also on another note I've [added the patch to Fabric](https://github.com/Fuzss/tinyskeletons/tree/main/1.21.8/Fabric/src/main/java/fuzs/tinyskeletons/fabric/mixin), but due to your Mixin it is broken (this is the same implementation used in Armor Foes, the source of which is not public yet).
So far my only option is to set `mixin.world.chunk_access=false` which is of course not ideal.

Honestly this is such a serious and hard to debug issue that it would be great in addition to fixing the Neo patch to also implement it on Fabric in Lithium itself.

issues.title: Entity Equipment tracking can leave player instances in memory

labels.name: F-has-workaround
labels.description: Flag: There is a workaround available

issues.body:
### Version Information
> Fabric 0.128.1+1.21.5
> Lithium 0.16.3
> Minecraft 1.21.5

### Expected Behavior

> References to players be removed when the player instance is no longer in use.

### Actual Behavior

> References to players via the PlayerEquipment are kept in memory if the player equipment had a shared item stack set to it.

### Reproduction Steps

Here is some example code to reproduce it: https://gist.github.com/ThatGravyBoat/aa9bcab7ea7846fd0dee8ffff782979a
If you run the game with that code and then do /bugreport 100000 it will create 100k instances of remote player with the same ItemStack this should in vanilla be fine and be cleared from the memory fairly fast but with Lithium they are kept around as the EntityEquipmentMixin subscribes itself to the ItemStack and when the player is removed that subscription is kept this would normally be fine as itd just be a list of equipment but PlayerEquipment extends EntityEquipment and stores a reference to the player in it causing it to keep a reference to the player and all its entities.

Specifically it has to not be the main hand as that is handled special by PlayerEquipment to set it to the player instance itself and not call the super of EntityEquipment where the mixin is.

Using a new instance of a player is common for displaying of the entity in screens with a different skin or equipment this causes those cases to have a memory leak. Current workaround is to copy the ItemStack before setting it to equipment.

issues.title: TNT minecart issue with b36 blocks
issues.body:
### Version Information

mc1.21.3-0.14.6-fabric

### Expected Behavior

TNT minecarts should consistently destroy cobblestone blocks in a big radius while they are in the b36  state during piston movement, as they have a blast resistance of 0 during that state.

### Actual Behavior

> The explosion sometimes destroys the blocks in a big radius *(what happens when blocks exploded are in b36 
> state)* and sometimes in a smaller radius like if the cobblestone kept its regular blast resistance of 6 instead of 
> taking 0 as they are moving thus in b36 form

### Reproduction Steps

> With a cobblestone generator, push a line of cobble and while its moving make it explode with a tnt minecart with an explosion power of 11.5 (drop the tnt minecart 75 blocks above the aimed cobble. Sometimes it will break the entire stream as if it had a blast resistance of 0 (cuz b36) but sometimes as if it had a blast resistance way higher even though it is in the b36 state

### Other Information

Tested the same exact setup in different versions and found that:
> In **1.20.1**(mc1.20.1-0.11.3-fabric) with lithium it works just fine
> In **1.20.4**(mc1.20.4-0.12.1)  / **1.21.3**(mc1.21.3-0.14.6-fabric) / **1.21.4**(mc1.21.4-0.15.3-fabric) with lithium it will sometimes break the blocks as if they had their basic blast resistance
*thats the versions i tested the setup in idk abt the other ones*
 But in the same versions as mentioned right above, just removing the lithium mod fixes the issue.


> A video to illustrate it: https://youtu.be/I6LJRu-8j0E (only the 3rd shot did what was supposed to happen yet blocks still disapeared in 2 separates tick idk why it might be a client issue too)

issues.title: Incompatability with Hopper Fill Bundles.

labels.name: E-will-not-fix
labels.description: Closed: This will not be worked on

labels.name: F-has-workaround
labels.description: Flag: There is a workaround available

issues.body:
### Version Information

> Lithium v0.15.1+mc1.21.4
> [Hopper-bundels-0.1.0-1.21.4](https://modrinth.com/mod/hoppers-fill-bundles/versions), [github](https://github.com/HydraheadHunter/Bundle-Hoppers) (Incompatability).

### Expected Behavior

> Hoppers Fill Bundles is a small mod which allows for hoppers to insert items into and extract items from bundles held in decorated pots. 
> When a hopper points into a decorated pot that has a bundle in it, the hopper should attempt to insert an item from its inventory into to decorated pot's bundle's `bundle_contents` item component every 'hopper tick.' 
> When a hopper draws from a decorated pot that has a bundle in it, the hopper should attempt to extract an item from the `bundle_contents` item component into its inventory every hopper tick. Once the bundle is empty, the hopper should then pull the bundle out of the decorated pot.

### Actual Behavior

> Lithium's rewrites of the hopper's functionality in a way that conflicts with the intended item insertion behavior. Items which should be inserted into the `bundle_contents` component instead sit in the hopper.
> Lithium does not conflict with the intended extraction behavior.

### Reproduction Steps

> Install both mods and the latest mc version-correct fabric api, at time of writing (0.119.2+1.21.4).
> Launch game and load a world.
> From the creative redstone menu, select the plain decorated pot and hopper.
> Point the hopper into the decorated pot.
> Put an empty bundle into the decorated pot.
> Fill the hopper with various partial stacks.
> Observe that the items do not flow out of the hopper and into the bundle.
>
> Close the game and uninstall Lithium.
> Relaunch the game and load the same world.
> Observe that the items now flow as intended.

### Other Information

> [Github issue which brought the incompatability to my attention](https://github.com/HydraheadHunter/Bundle-Hoppers/issues/1).
> Thank you for your time.

issues.title: `ChunkAwareBlockCollisionSweeper` outputs strange `VoxelShape` when `hideLastCollision` is false

labels.name: F-good-issue
labels.description: Flag: This is an example of a good issue report

issues.body:
## Summary

The `ChunkAwareBlockCollisionSweeper` might output `VoxelShape` in area oustide the given `AABB` box when `hideLastCollision` is false

## Environment

- mc1.21.1 / mc1.21.3 / mc1.21.4
- since at least `mc1.21.1-0.14.3`, to the current latest versions

## To reproduce

The following steps needs an IDE / java debugging environment to reproduce. Currently I haven't found a method to get a not-vanilla behavior caused by this issue

 The commit 414a96a3e0283acc8804862f6260a7f5d9009c61 (current latest commit in the develop branch) is used as the demonstration

1. Set a breakpoint [here](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium/blob/414a96a3e0283acc8804862f6260a7f5d9009c61/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/lithium/mixin/entity/collisions/movement/EntityMixin.java#L120) with a condition `entity instanceof net.minecraft.world.entity.item.PrimedTnt`
2. Create a void world, run the following commands in game

```
/setblock 15 10 15 minecraft:obsidian
/setblock 31 3 16 minecraft:obsidian
/summon tnt 15.5 1.0 15.9 {Motion:[0.0, 10.0, 0.01], fuse:1}
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3406336f-23fb-47a9-a4dc-d6465f3d8c4d)

3. The breakpoint should be hit. Now evaluate the following expression in the debugger (in the Server Thread of course)

```java
com.google.common.collect.Lists.newArrayList(new ChunkAwareBlockCollisionSweeper(world, entity, movementSpace, false))
```

4. Observe the expression result. You can find 2 suspicious `VoxelShape` inside, which should not be inside the result. It is worth noting that the Y coord of these 2 suspicious `VoxelShape` are exactly what the bounding box of the obsidian block at `(31, 3, 16)` is

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b090b76-9e57-4cdf-b08b-42a18c75d4f3)

> [!NOTE] 
> The TNT entity does move correctly without any issue since it constructs the `ChunkAwareBlockCollisionSweeper` with `hideLastCollision = true`
>
> The above setup is just to creating a example usage context of the `ChunkAwareBlockCollisionSweeper`

## Affects

The might affect the correctness of `LithiumEntityCollisions#getBlockCollisions` and `LithiumEntityCollisions#doesBoxCollideWithBlocks`

## Other information

It might be the cause of https://github.com/TISUnion/Carpet-TIS-Addition/issues/199

issues.title: Optimize ender dragon respawning
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Ender dragon respawning is notoriously laggy, and this prevents the usage of fast end stone farms that utilize the mechanic of end stone regenerating under the exit portal during dragon respawning. 
From what I understand, the lag is mainly caused by the search for exit portal blocks. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

[Carpet AMS Addition](https://github.com/Minecraft-AMS/Carpet-AMS-Addition) and [Optimized Dragon Respawn](https://modrinth.com/mod/optimized-dragon-respawn) provided an implementation of a fix, through caching previously found portal block locations. It was mentioned that vanilla parity could not be ensured within the documentation. Since the latter is no longer updated, it would be nice to have a more vanilla friendly version of this optimization within Lithium for newer versions.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Using Carpet AMS.

**Additional context**

Examples of farms requiring this optimization:
https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1iC4y1f7iX
https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1nj411r7zr

### Version Information

lithium-fabric-0.14.3-snapshot+mc1.21.1-build.92

I am the dev of Repurposed Structures mod that spawns additional structures in the world. It is expected that my structures generate without issues or any deadlocking.

### Actual Behavior

A user reported to me that their game is deadlocking where chunks stop loading and server logic stop running. After a long and tedious time of disabling mods, I narrowed down the issue to Lithium. Disabling Lithium stops the deadlocking
https://github.com/TelepathicGrunt/RepurposedStructures/issues/369

### Reproduction Steps

1. Put on Lithium and Repurposed Structures
2. Create a world with seed 2438457204829392124 
3. Teleport to 800, 120, 200
4. Move towards 1000, 120, 200
5. Notice that chunks stop loading. Mobs stop working.
6. Check latest.log to see no crash or errors.
7. Do a thread dump like this https://pastebin.com/raw/bNaTw5n4 and you will see no worldgen threads are running code. Just the server thread was trying to grab a chunk and is locked up waiting on that chunk.
8. Repeat by disabling either mod and see the issue does not happen.

issues.title: Critical MixinTransformerError During Client Bootstrap (NeoForge + Lithium Compatibility)
issues.body:
Description:
Minecraft crashes during bootstrap on version 1.21.4 with NeoForge 21.4.50-beta when running on macOS (M2 Pro) due to a MixinTransformerError related to Lithium mixins. The error occurs in HopperBlockEntityMixin, where LVT changes cause an injection failure in the ejectItems method.

Relevant Logs:
```
Caused by: org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.injection.throwables.InjectionError: 
LVT in net/minecraft/world/level/block/entity/HopperBlockEntity::ejectItems(...) 
has incompatible changes. Expected: [Lnet/minecraft/world/Container;, Lnet/minecraft/core/Direction;] 
Found: [Lnet/neoforged/neoforge/items/ContainerOrHandler;, Lnet/minecraft/world/Container;]
```

System Details:
	•	Minecraft Version: 1.21.4
	•	NeoForge Version: 21.4.50-beta
	•	Java: OpenJDK 21.0.3 (Microsoft)
	•	Mods: Lithium
	•	OS: macOS 15.2 (Apple M2 Pro)

Steps to Reproduce:
	1.	Install NeoForge 21.4.50-beta and Lithium mod.
	2.	Launch Minecraft 1.21.4 on macOS (M2 Pro).
	3.	Observe crash during bootstrap.

Additional Context:
The conflict seems to arise from differences in expected types for LVT during the injection in Lithium’s HopperBlockEntityMixin. This may require Lithium updates or a compatibility patch.

Crash Report:
[crash-2025-01-10_15.42.55-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18382258/crash-2025-01-10_15.42.55-client.txt)

issues.title: LittleTiles compatibility
issues.body:
Hey there,

I'm the author of LittleTiles and there are issues between our mods. I do some changes to the `Shapes` class in order to optimize performance. I do that in a way it should not affect other mods, as I only add a hook and change behavior for shape classes added by LittleTiles. Unfortunately this still breaks compatibility with lithium.

This can be solved by disabling these two features `mixin.shapes.specialized_shapes` and `mixin.entity.collisions`. The question if there is an easy way for me to set these two settings to false. Another option could also be for you to check whether LittleTiles is installed to disable these two features in question.

Let me know what you think about it.

In Regards
CreativeMD

**Note: This Issues exits only if "mixin.experimental" is set to true in lithium.properties**

- Lithium: 0.13.0 and above (Fixed)
- Lithium: 0.12.3, 0.12.4, 0.12.5 (Bug present)

1. Go to `C:\Users\(userName)\AppData\Roaming\.minecraft\config\lithium.properties`
     Note: (Replace (userName) with your user name)
2. Remove  "mixin.experimental" or change its value to false

issues.title: Wilder Wild Mesoglea Incompatibility
issues.body:
In Wilder Wild, there is a block called Mesoglea that acts as a static block of Water when waterlogged. When inside, there is a mixin to make "clipping" ignore other waterlogged Mesoglea blocks.
Lithium gets rid of this behavior, making the player target the Mesoglea block they're inside instead of whatever block they'd usually target.

Any help on how to fix this on our side (if possible) would be greatly appreciated as well.

Mixin: https://github.com/FrozenBlock/WilderWild/blob/master/src/main/java/net/frozenblock/wilderwild/mixin/block/mesoglea/BlockGetterMixin.java

labels.name: F-good-issue
labels.description: Flag: This is an example of a good issue report

labels.name: F-has-workaround
labels.description: Flag: There is a workaround available

issues.body:
### Version Information

lithium-fabric-mc1.21-0.12.5

### Expected Behavior

The comparator reading the shulker box should not output a signal if the shulker box is empty

### Actual Behavior

Sometimes when using a box unloader once the shulker box has been drained of all it's items, the comparator reading the box retains powered with a signal strength of 1. This does not occur without the mod, granted this has not been extensively tested but it usually breaks after 2 or 3 shulkers through the unloader and has not happened yet in Vanilla.

### Reproduction Steps

Not exactly 100% sure as I have only tested using a particular box unloader but other than that place a comparator facing away from a shulker box and then empty it, sometimes the empty shulker box will still have a signal strength of 1 read from it.

### Other Information

Tested on a private fabric server running Lithium, FerriteCore, C2ME, Bluemap, Jade, No-enderman-grief, and Spark

issues.title: Default config is incompatible with Fabrication minor mechanic
issues.body:
Hi,

Fabrication got a new feature recently for refueling furnace minecarts with hoppers, however it seems to be incompatible with lithium's default config for hopper optimisations.

https://github.com/FalsehoodMC/Fabrication/issues/718

In the config, disabling this rule fixes the issue: `mixin.block.hopper`
However, it seems that this disables every hopper optimisations when realistically, only this specific optimisation seems to be at fault:
https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium-fabric/blob/44f4330b9ab1cef568e80336d949c61386f747b9/src/main/java/me/jellysquid/mods/lithium/mixin/block/hopper/AbstractMinecartEntityMixin.java

(this is a conjecture from reading the code, I didn't actually debug the game or remove the optimisation manually to see if it fixes it)

Here is the relevant code from the Fabrication mod that's affected by the issue:
https://github.com/FalsehoodMC/Fabrication/blob/3.0/1.18/src/main/java/com/unascribed/fabrication/mixin/d_minor_mechanics/furnace_minecart_resupplying/MixinHopperBlockEntity.java#L31

------------------------

### Version Information

lithium-fabric-mc1.20.1-0.11.2

### Expected Behavior

Fabrication method should be triggered without having to disable every other optimisation, and ideally there should be a way for Fabrication to ask Lithium to change a config rule

### Actual Behavior

User has to disable all hopper optimisations for it to work

### Reproduction Steps

1- Install both mods
2- Enable "refueling furnace minecart" minor mechanic in Fabrication config
3- Place a rail down with a hopper with fuel pointing into it
4- Place furnace minecart on rail

### Other Information

Any info not outlined here can be found in the original Fabrication issue

issues.title: Lithium 0.12.x backport to 1.20.1
Allow externally changing Lithium's blockstate counters
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
[Noisium](https://modrinth.com/mod/noisium) and [Big Globe](https://modrinth.com/mod/big-globe) use a [performance optimisation](https://github.com/Steveplays28/noisium/blob/f4a44ab8ebdd69748f2f1da808d4c2913fd13183/src/main/java/io/github/steveplays28/noisium/mixin/NoiseChunkGeneratorMixin.java#L30-L52) during world generation that directly sets blocks in the palette instead of using `setBlock()`.
Currently, both Noisium and Big Globe increment vanilla's blockstate counters for parity, which works fine for vanilla, but not for Lithium. Lithium has custom blockstate counters that need to be set for underwater entities to behave correctly, such as squids and fish. If these blockstate counters are not set correctly during worldgen, it will cause underwater entities to fall and drown in water.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A way for other mods to increment Lithium's blockstate counters using an API. Moving the implementation out of the mixin would probably be required.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Calling Minecraft's vanilla blockstate counter method, instead of manually incrementing vanilla's blockstate counters. This is expensive though and would be very suboptimal.

**Additional context**
See also https://github.com/Steveplays28/noisium/issues/10. Included in that issue is a [video](https://streamable.com/4t71lf) showing the issue.

issues.title: [1.20.1 Fabric] Setting itemStack to null in EntityShapeContext breaks Bumblezone's brushable pollen block
issues.body:
Using lithium-fabric-mc1.20.1-0.11.2.jar and latest Bumblezone, attempting to brush a Suspicious Pile of Pollen block will do nothing. 

The problematic mixin:
https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium-fabric/blob/8df8ae68c961ac7ee92172168dc10966b3afc2c5/src/main/java/me/jellysquid/mods/lithium/mixin/shapes/lazy_shape_context/EntityShapeContextMixin.java#L69

The issue comes down to me needing to use the EntityShapeContext's itemstack field directly so I can check if the item is in my brushing allowed tag. The isHolding method is no sufficient to my needs. However, Lithium sets this field to null which causes my block to never be brushed because it thinks player held item is null which is wrong.
https://github.com/TelepathicGrunt/Bumblezone/blob/cf5e4c67ba5de7713458651f05d888cc884b4752/common/src/main/java/com/telepathicgrunt/the_bumblezone/blocks/PileOfPollenSuspicious.java#L126

I originally got told about this issue because in past Bumblezone version, this conflict crashed my mod due to Canary copying the same mixin from lithium. I put out a null check fix but realized now that it means while the crash is stopped, the block is no longer brushable. I checked Fabric and Lithium also causes the issue with the mixin
https://github.com/AbdElAziz333/Canary/issues/182
https://github.com/TelepathicGrunt/Bumblezone/issues/299

I have suspicion on if this null field setting is even giving any tangible performance benefit... In general, itemstacks should never be null. As of now, I need to hack around Lithium to get the actual held item from the context again. What I may have to do is call isHolding directly once with a dummy input to force Lithium to init itemstack. Then get the field. 

I wanted to grab the item directly from the context in case other mods make their own context with the itemstack set directly like a fake player or some sort of autobrushing machine which is why I can't assume that I can call `((LivingEntity)this.entity).getMainHandStack()` myself.

issues.title: Overworld is removed from world_gen_settings when used with WilderWild and custom ChunkGenerator class
issues.body:
The base issue came up in this report: quiqueck/BCLib#113

I am still not sure what is happening, but I figured out some things while testing. The crash happens when BClib, Lithium and WilderWild are installed. But I think the issue is not with WilderWild, but instead with QuiltDataFixes in general.

Let me explain the setting:
BCLib is defining a custom ChunkGenerator class, that is registered as `bclib:betterx` to the builtin [ChunkGenerator Registry](https://github.com/quiqueck/BCLib/blob/2e42a06d8af8907e066d9c053a073e0c7a05846f/src/main/java/org/betterx/bclib/mixin/common/ChunkGeneratorsMixin.java#L23). I checked, and the registry contains the codec reference. We use this Generator for the Nether and the End. The overworld is using the vanilla ChunkGenerator.

Then there is [`QuiltDataFixes.updateWithAllFixers`](https://github.com/QuiltMC/quilt-standard-libraries/blob/1.20/library/misc/datafixerupper/src/main/java/org/quiltmc/qsl/datafixerupper/impl/QuiltDataFixesInternalsImpl.java#L70), which is used by the Mod [WilderWild](https://github.com/FrozenBlock/WilderWild/blob/1.20/src/main/java/net/frozenblock/wilderwild/WilderWild.java#L135). It just registers some simple fixes, as far as I can tell, nothing that is messing with the dimensions of a world.

Using BCLib and WilderWild will not cause any issues. When I add Lithium to the mix, the Overworld (remember the only dimension that does not use the custom ChunkGenerator) is deleted when the DataFixerers for `DataFixTypes.WORLD_GEN_SETTINGS` are executed in `LevelStorage.readGeneratorProperties`.

With and without Lithium, the DataFixer will issue an error:
> Unsupported key: bclib:betterx; Unsupported key: bclib:betterx

(which indicates, that there is a problem reading the custom ChunkGenerator, which is caused by a Vanilla DataFixer called `MissingDimensionFix`). When I create a new world with BCLib that does not include the custom ChunkGenerators, the error is not produced (as expected) and the overworld is not deleted. But as I said, without Lithium the missing generator type does not cause any issues, except for the error message.

Which leads me to suspect, that there is an interior problem between Lithium and QuiltDataFixes? However, I am not sure if this is caused by Lithium or QSL...

To confirm that the root cause of the problem is `MissingDimensionFix` (which is hard coded to the vanilla generator types), I went and added some Mixins, that add the custom type to the Vanilla DataFixers. This indeed solves the issue. However that feels quite intrusive. 

Since there are other mods out there that intruduce custom ChunkGenerators as well, this might be an issue worth looking into?

issues.title: OrderedTickQueue: resize logic?
issues.body:
- Link to file on develop branch: [OrderedTickQueue.java](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium-fabric/blob/develop/src/main/java/me/jellysquid/mods/lithium/common/world/scheduler/OrderedTickQueue.java)
- Current version, permalink: [OrderedTickQueue.java @ 81c3253a75](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium-fabric/blob/81c3253a75f7eb518334df5e93b2110966023766/src/main/java/me/jellysquid/mods/lithium/common/world/scheduler/OrderedTickQueue.java)

https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium-fabric/blob/81c3253a75f7eb518334df5e93b2110966023766/src/main/java/me/jellysquid/mods/lithium/common/world/scheduler/OrderedTickQueue.java#L118-L138

Resize is supposed to shrink the array to reduce memory consumption. A couple things that made me stumble:

If `size` is 0, then following `copyArray()` with size=0 will allocate `new OrderedTick[0];`. At first I thought this could be improved (instead: resize to an initial size), but with the current code it seems *intentional* to actually get a size 0 array.

Upon further inspection, it appears the entire class could be rewritten to reduce the amount of reallocations, because it already tracks first/lastIndex? Since the backing array is kept private and all accesses happen through the interface, the functions could be rewritten to rely on the indexes more and update them, rather than resizing/copying the array. Then the reallocation may only happen when the occupied size drops below a threshold (e.g. in removeNullsAndConsumed) or new values are added. Sorting would operate on a part of the array etc. (There are no null holes, right?)

Further, if the array happens to be resized to zero, the size increases in `offer(...)` will start very slow, despite being powers of two (0 → 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 (initial size constant)). The rewrite based on indexes would allow to have a backing array of any minimum size while not performing any operations when it's isEmpty().

I think the entire `copyArray` function can be replaced with [Arrays.copyOf​(T[] original, int newLength)](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Arrays.html#copyOf(T[],int)), no? ([jdk source](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/0cbfbc400aac53b098a3d8a7dda1aec2180a47a7/src/java.base/share/classes/java/util/Arrays.java#L3509)).

Similarly, the manual looping in L123 to set null could be replaced with Arrays.fill(...) - that's just for readability, if anything.

issues.title: Move NearbyEntityListener::forEachChunkInRangeChange call to after Fabric Api's ServerEntityEvents#ENTITY_LOAD runs
issues.body:
Hey there, so I have a couple mods that add additional goals to some vanilla entities which are of type `AvoidEntityGoal`, e.g. make villagers avoid/flee from skeletons. I do this using Fabric Api's `ServerEntityEvents#ENTITY_LOAD` callback, since this seems to be the best place for such a thing without having to resort to custom mixins.

When doing this with Lithium installed, the game crashes when my new goals are trying to be added in `ServerEntityEvents#ENTITY_LOAD` with the following exception:
`java.lang.IllegalStateException: Cannot add sublisteners after listening range was set!` ([full crash-report](https://gist.github.com/Fuzss/9fde0233fa9ee34c4e44d29e53af2c44))

This happens since `NearbyEntityListenerMulti#range` is set in [`NearbyEntityListenerMulti::getChunkRange`](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium-fabric/blob/740ffc7a77894c4b3e394ffca0e43e8594e3e364/src/main/java/me/jellysquid/mods/lithium/common/entity/nearby_tracker/NearbyEntityListenerMulti.java#L29) which runs before the Fabric Api callback.

Would it be possible to set the range field after Fabric Api's callback has run, either by moving the injection in [`ServerEntityManagerMixin`](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium-fabric/blob/740ffc7a77894c4b3e394ffca0e43e8594e3e364/src/main/java/me/jellysquid/mods/lithium/mixin/ai/nearby_entity_tracking/ServerEntityManagerMixin.java#L33) or by migrating to the Fabric Api callback at a phase that runs after `fabric:default`?

issues.title: [1.19.2] Several crashes from several mixins constant
issues.body:
Before i add all the required details, I wanted to make sure its fine that I post what i'd like to post....

In my modpack, Another Quality Modpack 2, for 1.19.2, my official servers have been consistently crashing 6-10 times a day, all watchdog crashes from lithium mixins. There is no reproduction steps, it just happens randomly. 

After disabling the following mixins, ( I disabled one at a time to see if it would eliminate that consistent crash for the specified mixin in the crash log) the crash stopped occurring 

```
mixin.world.chunk_access=false
mixin.world.block_entity_ticking=false
mixin.world.chunk_inline_block_access=false
mixin.ai.pathing=false
mixin.alloc.chunk_ticking=false
```

The above mixins are the sum of all that work. 

Most recent one was mixin.alloc.chunk_ticking which happened 4 times in the last 30 hours. After disabling that mixin, no more crash.

---

I have tons, and tons of crash reports going back 30 days each crash report in relation to each mixin (shoutouts to MixinTrace mod). Should I upload these? What would be the best way to deliver these logs to you so you can be aware of these issues?

issues.title: Separate config for ticking lit/unlit campfires
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Mods like Survival Campfires and Totally Lit track campfires' burn time with NBT data, sleeping lit campfires break these mods.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Split `mixin.world.block_entity_ticking.sleeping.campfire` into `mixin.world.block_entity_ticking.sleeping.campfire.lit` and `mixin.world.block_entity_ticking.sleeping.campfire.unlit`

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Or maybe it's possible to provide a way (nbt tag?) for modders to prevent campfires/block entities from sleeping? This could be even better because most of the time only player-placed campfires need to be ticked.

issues.title: Seperate alloc.enum_values mixins

labels.name: F-good-issue
labels.description: Flag: This is an example of a good issue report

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In order to disable `mixin/alloc/enum_values/RedstoneWireBlockMixin`, I need to add `"mixin.alloc.enum_values": false` inside my mod's `fabric.mod.json` file. However, doing so also disables all other mixins in the same `enum_values` folder. Because of this, I find myself required to disable AI mixins (`mixin.ai.task.launch` and `mixin.ai.task.replace_streams`) which have nothing to do with my mod. Not disabling these AI mixins gives errors pointing towards `mixin.ai.task.launch` and `mixin.ai.task.replace_streams`.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Place each file in the `mixin/alloc/enum_values` folder into their own folder so that users can disable them individually.

issues.title: Hopper does not pull items from modded containers that subclass vanilla containers and override their functions without super calls

labels.name: S-info-needed
labels.description: Status: Further information is needed to diagnose this issue

issues.body:
## Instructions

This is very similar to issue https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium-fabric/issues/417, albeit in a different nature.

Most notably I do not use Fabric Carpet here. 

Hoppers with Mythic Metals Decorations do not work properly when Lithium is installed. The issue only seems to happen on extraction rather than inserting into the containers.

I have tried both using Fabrics Item Transfer API (see https://github.com/Noaaan/MythicMetalsDecorations/blob/333319ba22f1d65bf3caa50e168ce05a8cc4d763/src/main/java/nourl/mythicmetalsdecorations/MythicMetalsDecorations.java#L66).

My containers do support `LithiumInventory` (via https://github.com/Noaaan/MythicMetalsDecorations/blob/1.19/src/main/java/nourl/mythicmetalsdecorations/mixin/MythicChestBlockEntityLithiumCompatMixin.java#L11), yet the hoppers do not respect the chests.

------------------------

### Version Information

Using lithium-fabric-mc1.19.3-0.10.4 and Mythic Metals Decorations 0.5.1+1.19.3 (unreleased), and is reproducible outside of a development environment. 
~~This issue also happens with lithium-fabric-mc1.19.2-0.10.2 and mythicmetals-decorations 0.5.1+1.19.2 (also unreleased)~~
~~Turns out this is not the case, my apologies.~~
Tested it against the backport of lithium-fabric-mc.1.19.2**-0.10.4** and it does NOT work. This might exclusively be an issue with the later versions of Lithium (>0.10.2).

### Expected Behavior

The items from the top hopper should fall through to the bottom hopper

### Actual Behavior

The items stop inside the chest. 

### Reproduction Steps
- Place two hoppers, one above and below the chest.
- Place an item in the top hopper
- Check the bottom hopper for items


### Other Information

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4163353/216141822-007d48eb-f997-4256-b7bb-4a1781ba372d.png)

If the state of the hopper changes (for example by updating the stack, placing a block above/below it), then the hopper will start extracting items again. 

Full modlist:
- https://pastebin.com/tXLyLEpN

TLDR:
- Fabric API
- Mythic Metals Decorations, 
- Lithium
- Smooth Boot
- LazyDFU
- their dependencies

issues.body:
The issue is splitted from #442

#### Instructions

The following tnt duper behavior changes when the tnt entity is nearby a chunk border

#### Reproduction Steps

1. Install [fabric-carpet](https://github.com/gnembon/fabric-carpet) mod
2. Build 2 of the tnt duper in the following image in a correct direction
    - The coordinate of the sticky piston are `-2 -58 59` and `-12 -58 59`

   ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28978806/214572408-adb670d2-0743-458e-845b-83e9c8dc0418.png)

    ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28978806/214572056-7f884f63-04bf-4936-bd11-3f426924cfe9.png)

3. Use fabric-carpet's command `/carpet hardcodeTNTangle 4.457099494579702` to override tnt initial velocity
4. Activate the tnt duper with 4gt pulse every 8gt

#### Behavior

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28978806/214571460-af1401fe-14fd-465d-bc7b-7f7f2332ec3f.png)

**Expected** behavior: Both of these 2 tnt dupers launch tnt on retract (this is also the vanilla behavior)

**Actual** behavior: The left duper in the image doesn't launch tnt, which behavior wrongly. Only the right one launch tnt

### Version Information

Reproduced with

| MC version | lithium version | carpet version |
| ---------- | --------------- | -------------- |
| 1.18.2     | 0.10.3          | 1.4.66         |
| 1.19       | 0.8.1           | 1.4.79         |
| 1.19.3     | 0.10.4          | 1.4.93         |

### Other Information

The behavior is locational. The wrong behavior only happens nearby chunk border

issues.title: [1.15~1.17] Inconsistent tnt movement behavior with vanilla, if tnt moves and collides with a block with <1E-7 intersection

labels.name: E-will-not-fix
labels.description: Closed: This will not be worked on

labels.name: F-good-issue
labels.description: Flag: This is an example of a good issue report

issues.body:
#### Instructions

Yeah, some fun 1E-7 thing I guess

In vanilla, tnt is able to move and slightly collide without a block without considered being blocked by the block. Here slightly means < 1E-7 block. With lithium in specific mc version range, that behavior is changed

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28978806/214312221-166a3258-8646-450c-bbe0-3d419948ffe5.png)

------------------------

### Reproduction Steps

1. Place the following blocks in the correct direction. Command block command: `summon tnt ~1 ~-0.5 ~ {Motion: [0d, 0d, 0.01000005d], Fuse:80}`

  ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28978806/214313790-e6dc2668-f793-4f1e-9668-9b0bc14ff936.png)

2. Press the button, watch the summoned tnt

**Vanilla** behavior: TNT gets launched by the slime block

**Lithium** behavior: TNT falls straight down

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28978806/214314781-cd3d3eab-3a0b-42c3-bf9a-95e7c91ed42e.png)

### Version Information

Tested with

| MC version | lithium version | matches vanilla?   |
| ---------- | --------------- | ------------------ |
| 1.15.2     | 0.4.6           | :x:                |
| 1.16.4/5   | 0.6.4           | :x:                |
| 1.17.1     | 0.7.5           | :x:                |
| 1.18.2     | 0.10.3          | :x:                |
| 1.19       | 0.8.0           | :heavy_check_mark: |
| 1.19.3     | 0.10.4          | :heavy_check_mark: |

Edited: this table contains incorrect result. See https://github.com/CaffeineMC/lithium/issues/442#issuecomment-1403067754 for updated result

### Other Information

This issue might affect other kinds of entity as well, tnt is just an example

There might be some unfound issues which are also related to this 1E-7 thing, e.g. if the piston extends slower and the tnt collides with the slimeblock, what tnt's z coord will be, sill .51000005, or another adjusted value

Potential vanilla bug exposed, cuz tnt being launched doesn't make any sense. This vanilla behavior happens in 1.14+, and lithium covers this vanilla issue until 1.19

Some research of this issue can be found in https://docs.qq.com/doc/DU0N0elZsTVN0TXNo (in Chinese tho)

Minecraft bug report: https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-259354

labels.description: Flag: There is a workaround available

issues.body:
### Version Information

lithium-fabric-mc1.19.2-0.10.4
Charm-fabric-1.19.2.-4.4.4


One of Charm's added tweaks is the ability to right click a shulker over an item in the inventory to store the item(s) away in the shullker without having to place it. Unfortunately, it appears Lithium's sleeping shulkers mixin disables this functionality as well as the ability to see the inventory of the shulker. 

There's a possibility it does the same with mods with similar features/tweaks. 
Current workaround is to just disable the sleeping shulkers mixin in the config file.
